RDT allocation (rdt_a: cat_l2 cat_l3 cdp_l2 cdp_l3 mba) — resctrl classes are available but left off: the balloons policy ships control.rdt.enable: false because enabling it rewrites the host's /sys/fs/resctrl. To opt in, mount resctrl on the host (mount -t resctrl resctrl /sys/fs/resctrl) and set control.rdt.enable: true in nri-balloons.yml; usePodQoSAsDefaultClass then gives BestEffort/Burstable/Guaranteed pods 33%/66%/100% of the L3. To revert, set control.rdt.enable: false in nri-balloons.yml, then sudo umount /sys/fs/resctrl

noisy-neighbour isolation: rdt-mba — CAT + MBA can cap a neighbour's cache share and DRAM bandwidth through the RDT opt-in above (resctrl mounted: no); the shipped classes set cache shares only, so add mbAllocation: {all: ["50%"]} to the BestEffort class for bandwidth; the classes run inside the NRI balloons policy, which up deploys on hybrid or multi-NUMA hosts only

sections.good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token
sections.name: CPU frequency (driver intel_pstate, mode active)

sections.good: max_freq_khz at initial_max_freq_khz and min_freq_khz at initial_min_freq_khz: the hardware (UFS, or ELC on TPMI parts) picks the uncore clock inside the full range. A floor pinned high for decode is unproven (EXPERIMENTS.md H29, INCONCLUSIVE), so it is not suggested
sections.name: Uncore frequency (intel_uncore_frequency)

sections.good: for latency-critical serving, no idle state whose exit latency is large next to a token step; for throughput or power budgets, leave them all on
sections.name: CPU idle states (intel_idle, intel_idle.max_cstate=9)

sections.good: no throttle time under load: the package stays below its TCC activation point (TjMax minus the TCC offset), so cores keep the frequency they request
sections.name: CPU thermal throttling
sections.src: kernel source drivers/thermal/intel/therm_throt.c (thermal_throttle/*), drivers/thermal/intel/int340x_thermal/processor_thermal_device.c (tcc_offset_degree_celsius), drivers/hwmon/coretemp.c (tempN_crit = TjMax), Intel SDM vol. 4 335592-093 (IA32_THERM_STATUS 19CH, IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS 1B1H, MSR_CORE_PERF_LIMIT_REASONS 64FH in table 2-39)

sections.good: none while serving: a reason names what held the die or a CPU below its requested frequency
sections.name: TPMI performance limit reasons

sections.good: PL1 (long_term) at or above the thermal spec power (TDP, reported as constraint_0_max_power_uw) so sustained inference is not clamped below spec; PL1 decides the clock under a long run, PL2 only covers short bursts. On a package that thermally throttles, a PL1 far above TDP only moves the limit from power to temperature
sections.name: CPU package power limits (RAPL)
sections.src: https://docs.kernel.org/power/powercap/powercap.html, kernel source drivers/powercap/intel_rapl_common.c (PL1 max_power = PKG_POWER_INFO thermal spec power)

sections.good: enabled = always or madvise (fewer TLB misses over multi-GB weight and KV buffers), defrag != always (no allocation stalls mid-request)
sections.name: Transparent huge pages

sections.good: 0 unless a server is configured to use hugetlbfs — reserved pages cannot be used for anything else, and OpenVINO, PyTorch and llama.cpp do not use them by default
sections.name: Reserved huge pages (hugetlbfs)

sections.good: the model plus KV cache fits in MemAvailable with headroom and nothing is swapped; swapped-out buffers fault back in at random-I/O speed
sections.name: Memory and swap

sections.good: modules at the platform's plan-of-record (POR) speed for how the slots are populated; single-stream CPU and iGPU decode is bound by DRAM bandwidth. Memory errors counted by an EDAC driver
